case.initial_facts:
A man in his late 70s has several months of painless left-scrotal swelling without systemic symptoms. He has no known asbestos exposure and previously worked in an office. No relevant trauma, chronic hydrocele, radiation, family cancer history or smoking is reported.
The swelling transilluminates and preoperative ultrasound was reported as an uncomplicated hydrocele. At elective surgery, red friable nodules are unexpectedly seen on the tunica. Histology, tumour markers, staging and subsequent treatment are not yet supplied.
The published descriptions of subtle preoperative mural nodularity are inconsistent between the prose and image caption; the evaluation does not provide a definite nodularity finding from that scan.

case.reference: Atypical friable tunical nodules warrant tissue diagnosis and specialist review despite an initial uncomplicated hydrocele report. Absence of exposure history does not exclude malignancy. Keep malignant, reactive and other relevant alternatives provisional until histology is available; do not demand the later named rare subtype. The disputed ultrasound wording must not become a scoring requirement. Later selected surveillance does not establish a universal management rule.
